title: Third stage, puerperium, lactation, forceps/vacuum, cord prolapse, VBAC
subject: OBGY
anchor: Active management of the third stage: oxytocin 10 IU IM within 1 minute of birth, controlled cord traction, uterine massage; delay cord clamping 1–3 minutes.
Puerperium lasts 6 weeks; the fundus is at the umbilicus after delivery, falls ~1 cm/day and is no longer palpable per abdomen by about 2 weeks.
Cord prolapse: relieve pressure on the cord, then immediate caesarean (category 1) unless vaginal delivery is imminent.

points: Retained placenta: no delivery by 30 minutes (WHO) needs manual removal under anaesthesia with prophylactic antibiotics.
Signs of placental separation: gush of blood, lengthening of cord, uterus becomes firm, globular and rises (Calkins).
Cord prolapse management: knee–chest or Sims (head-down left lateral) position, elevate the presenting part manually, bladder filling (500–750 ml), tocolysis (terbutaline) as a bridge to caesarean.

VBAC/TOLAC: success ~60–80%; contraindications include prior classical caesarean, prior uterine rupture; the most consistent sign of rupture is abnormal CTG; uterine rupture risk with TOLAC is under 1%.
Postpartum IUCD (Cu-T 380A) can be inserted within 48 hours of delivery (best within 10 minutes of placental delivery) or after 4 weeks.
Puerperal sepsis: polymicrobial; group A Streptococcus is the most dangerous organism; give broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (clindamycin + gentamicin / piperacillin-tazobactam).

traps.fix: Avoid vacuum before 34 weeks (subgaleal bleed, intracranial haemorrhage).
Intervene at 30 minutes of the third stage per WHO.

title: Antenatal care, USG dating, aneuploidy screening, NTD, hyperemesis, abortion and MTP Act
subject: OBGY
anchor: Crown-rump length in the first trimester is the most accurate dating method (±5–7 days up to 13+6 weeks).
NT scan 11–13+6 weeks; level II (anomaly) scan 18–20 weeks; Td/Tdap and iron-folate are core ANC interventions.
MTP Act (amended 2021): up to 20 weeks one RMP; 20–24 weeks two RMPs for special categories; beyond 24 weeks only for substantial fetal abnormality by Medical Board.

Down syndrome pattern

AFP low, hCG high, uE3 low
Highest sensitivity screen for T21; confirm positives with amniocentesis

head: Finding
Time
rows: ~1500–2000 IU/L: sac should be visible; absent = ectopic suspicion

points: Folic acid 0.4 mg daily from preconception; 4 mg/day if previous NTD pregnancy (India and US guidance); NTD screen: raised maternal serum AFP and acetylcholinesterase in amniotic fluid.
Hyperemesis gravidarum: IV fluids; give thiamine before glucose (Wernicke); first-line drug combination doxylamine–pyridoxine.
Medical abortion in India: mifepristone 200 mg followed 24–48 h later by misoprostol 800 mcg, approved up to 9 weeks (63 days).
Recurrent pregnancy loss: antiphospholipid syndrome is the commonest treatable cause (low-dose aspirin + LMWH); cervical insufficiency treated with McDonald cerclage at 12–14 weeks.

Superfecundation = two ova fertilised at separate coital acts within one cycle (different fathers possible); superfetation = fertilisation of a second ovum in a pregnant woman at a later cycle (very rare).
India's PMSMA (9th of every month) offers a free specialist ANC check; at least 4 ANC visits.

traps.fix: CRL is more accurate than LMP and BPD.

traps.stem: Folic acid dose after a previous child with NTD
traps.fix: 4 mg daily from at least 1 month before conception through 12 weeks.

title: Preterm labour, PROM/PPROM, FGR, amniotic fluid disorders
subject: OBGY
anchor: Preterm labour before 37 weeks: tocolysis (nifedipine), antenatal steroids 24–34 weeks, magnesium sulphate for neuroprotection under 32 weeks.
PPROM: avoid digital examination; confirm with pooling/nitrazine/ferning or placental alpha-microglobulin; antibiotics erythromycin + amoxicillin/ampicillin.
FGR with Doppler sequence: raised umbilical artery PI → absent EDF → reversed EDF → abnormal ductus venosus; deliver by gestation and Doppler stage.

Notes
rows: Only before 32 weeks (premature ductus closure, oligohydramnios)
Avoid orally; maternal tachycardia, hypokalaemia, pulmonary oedema

head: Item
Value / cause
rows: AFI <5 cm or deepest vertical pocket <2 cm
Renal agenesis/obstructive uropathy, PPROM, FGR, post-term, NSAIDs/ACE inhibitors
Idiopathic, diabetes, oesophageal/duodenal atresia, anencephaly, hydrops
Complication of prolonged early-onset oligohydramnios (Potter sequence)

points: Antenatal corticosteroids: betamethasone 12 mg IM 24 h apart ×2 doses (or dexamethasone 6 mg IM 12-hourly ×4).
Cervical length <25 mm at 16–24 weeks predicts preterm birth; vaginal progesterone 200 mg nightly reduces risk in short cervix.
PPROM with infection signs (maternal fever, tachycardia, fetal tachycardia, tender uterus) = chorioamnionitis: antibiotics and delivery.
SGA = EFW <10th centile; FGR adds growth failure or abnormal Doppler (AC/EFW <3rd centile or <10th with Doppler change).
Middle cerebral artery low PI with raised cerebroplacental ratio inversion = brain sparing.
Polyhydramnios treated by serial amnioreduction or indomethacin (before 32 weeks).

traps.fix: Avoid co-amoxiclav (necrotising enterocolitis); use erythromycin + amoxicillin/ampicillin.

title: Genital prolapse, stress incontinence, urinary fistula
subject: OBGY
anchor: Prolapse is staged by POP-Q; main support of the uterus is the cardinal (Mackenrodt) ligament complex with uterosacral ligaments.
Surgery by situation: uterine prolapse with elongated cervix = Manchester; vault prolapse = sacrocolpopexy (gold standard) or sacrospinous fixation; frail elderly not sexually active = colpocleisis.
Obstetric VVF (obstructed labour) is common in India; continuous painless leak; methylene blue three-swab test; ureterovaginal needs IVP/CT urogram.

tables.title: POP-Q stages

Leading edge
rows: Within 1 cm above or below hymen
More than 1 cm beyond hymen but not complete (< TVL – 2 cm)

tables.title: Incontinence
head: Type
Mechanism
Treatment
rows: Urethral hypermobility / sphincter weakness; leak on cough
Pelvic floor exercises; mid-urethral sling (TVT/TOT) is the standard surgery; Burch colposuspension
Bladder training; anticholinergics (oxybutynin) or mirabegron; botulinum toxin

points: Fistula repair: fresh small fistula catheter drainage for 2–4 weeks; established fistula repaired when tissues are healthy (often after about 3 months, earlier repair is acceptable); Latzko or flap repairs; Martius flap for complex fistulae.
Cystocele and rectocele are anterior and posterior vaginal wall prolapse; enterocele is herniation of the pouch of Douglas.
Pessary (ring) is the non-surgical option; treat vaginal atrophy with local oestrogen.
First-line treatment for stress incontinence is pelvic floor muscle training.

traps.fix: Sacrocolpopexy is the gold standard for apical (vault) prolapse.
Three-swab (tampon) test distinguishes VVF from ureterovaginal fistula.

Methylene blue dye test (three-swab test), cystoscopy.

title: Mullerian anomalies, puberty, menopause/HRT, vaginitis and PID
subject: OBGY
anchor: Septate uterus is the commonest Mullerian anomaly (poorest reproductive outcome; hysteroscopic septal resection).
Puberty sequence: thelarche → pubarche → growth spurt → menarche; precocious puberty <8 years, delayed if no breast development by 13 or no menarche by 15.
HRT: combined oestrogen + progestogen if uterus present; oestrogen alone after hysterectomy.

points: Premature ovarian insufficiency: amenorrhoea before 40 with FSH >25 IU/L on two occasions 4 weeks apart.
HRT contraindications: breast or endometrial cancer, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, active venous thromboembolism, active liver disease.
Tibolone has oestrogenic, progestogenic and androgenic effects; fezolinetant (NK3 antagonist) is a non-hormonal option for vasomotor symptoms.
Fitz-Hugh–Curtis syndrome: perihepatitis with violin-string adhesions in PID (chlamydia, gonorrhoea).
Sequelae of PID: tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain.

title: Infertility work-up, semen analysis, ART, OHSS, missed pills, DMPA and IUCD pregnancy
subject: OBGY
anchor: Tubal patency: HSG in the follicular phase (day 7–10, after bleeding stops); laparoscopic chromopertubation is the gold standard.
WHO 2021 (6th edition) semen lower reference limits: volume 1.4 ml, concentration 16 million/ml, total 39 million, total motility 42%, progressive 30%, vitality 54%, normal forms 4%.
Letrozole is now first-line ovulation induction in PCOS; clomiphene 50 mg days 2–5.

points: Hysterosalpingography: contraindicated in active pelvic infection and pregnancy; give antibiotics if hydrosalpinx suspected.
OHSS: ascites, haemoconcentration, hypovolaemia; severe form needs admission, albumin, thromboprophylaxis; avoid hCG trigger in high risk.
Cu-T 380A is effective for 10 years; LNG-IUS 52 mg is licensed for 5 years (extended to 8 in some regions).
DMPA: delayed return to fertility, bone density loss, irregular bleeding; safe in lactation after 6 weeks.
Basal body temperature rises 0.3–0.5 °C after ovulation (progesterone).
